- When sentiment turns sharply negative (e.g., -0.67+ drop) and news volume drops to 0, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast by 1–2% of recent range.
- After a sentiment spike (e.g., +1.00), model often overshoots and fails to mean-revert — cap forecast at 1–2% above recent high.
- If sentiment change is negative and news volume is low, model underreacts — adjust forecast down by 0.5–1.5% of 30d mean.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive but news volume is low, model overestimates — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0%.
- Model consistently overestimates early in 30d horizon when sentiment is rising — apply 1–2% downward bias for first 5–7 days.
- If sentiment is flat or declining over 3–5 days, model often fails to recognize mean reversion — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day of flat sentiment.
- When sentiment is high and news volume is high, model tends to overreact — cap forecast at 1–2% below recent peak.
